summary.headline: DEE Development FY26 revenue rose 38% to Rs 1,142 Cr and PAT 76.9% to Rs 77.2 Cr; order book Rs 2,040 Cr with FY27 inflow guided above Rs 2,000 Cr.
summary.overview: FY26 was the first year after most of the growth capex cycle, with Anjar fabrication and the seamless pipe plant commissioned. Q4 FY26 revenue was Rs 361.6 Cr (+26.3% YoY) and PAT Rs 27.7 Cr, against a high Q4 FY25 base that included Q3 spillover. Management split the business into core (piping, heavy fabrication) and non-core (power, biomass pallets), with core EBITDA of Rs 210.5 Cr (+64.2%) excluding non-core losses. The company guided to a Rs 1,500 Cr revenue commitment for FY27, a Rs 2,500 Cr revenue target by FY30, and a consolidated EBITDA margin above 19%, while the Malwa Power tariff revision and the Thailand HRSG job-work order were the main new items.

segments.name: Core business (piping, heavy fabrication, others)
segments.commentary: FY26 core EBITDA incl. other income Rs 210.5 Cr, up 64.2%, driven by execution, utilisation and operating leverage. Management expects consolidated EBITDA margin above 19%, with heavy fabrication margins similar to piping.

segments.name: Non-core power (Malwa Power)
segments.commentary: Tariff revised to Rs 5.22/kWh from Rs 3.5/kWh with retrospective recovery of about Rs 5.52 Cr; Rs 5 Cr of the retrospective benefit is in the quarter per analyst Q&A. Appellate challenge pending; plant still carries a qualified audit opinion.

segments.name: Non-core biomass pallets
segments.commentary: Biomass pallet facility recently commissioned, expected to offset current cash burn. Combined power and pallet revenue guided at about Rs 47.71 Cr in FY27.

segments.name: DEE Thailand (HRSG job work)
segments.commentary: Unit works purely on job-work basis; about 60% of its roughly 14,500 capacity reserved for HRSG orders, with revenue of about Rs 150 Cr per year implied. Management said no capex is needed for this order beyond minor machinery.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue commitment of Rs 1,500 Cr, described as conservative; management said it may exceed this.
FY27 order inflow expected above Rs 2,000 Cr, about 60% power and 30-40% oil and gas, with 60-65% domestic and 35-40% export.
Revenue target of Rs 2,500 Cr by FY30, which could come earlier if order flow accelerates.
Consolidated EBITDA margin to stay above 19%, though percentage margin in heavy fabrication may fall as material-supply jobs rise, while value increases.
Working capital cycle target about 180 days in FY27 (inventory days down 15-20, payable days to 70-75, debtor days 95-100); CFO later said around 200 days.
FY27 capex guided at Rs 20-30 Cr, with a possible new capacity expansion (nuclear and other sectors) still on the drawing board.
capex_capacity: Anjar pipe fabrication facility fully operational; seamless pipe plant commissioned during FY26.
Seamless plant utilisation expected to reach about 60-70% in FY27; Anjar fabrication expected to reach optimal levels in FY27.
Capacity reserved for Nooter Eriksen at 60% of HRSG piping capacity; Thailand unit about 14,500 capacity, 60% reserved for HRSG.
Approvals for P-91/P-92 seamless pipe expected shortly, which would allow near-full domestic supply for power jobs.
Management is evaluating new capacity for nuclear and other sectors; no decision yet, and capacity to be sustainable for 10-15 years.
demand_pricing: Management expects GE gas turbine piping orders to surge; GE HRSG order book is already sizeable, with Nooter Eriksen taking 60% of capacity.
Discussions ongoing with Siemens for similar HRSG capacity arrangements; competition is mainly Korean and Turkish players.
Current power-sector order book above Rs 1,000 Cr (around Rs 1,200 Cr); L1 of about Rs 210 Cr in power.
Domestic thermal ordering depends on BHEL, which management described as slow; L&T moving faster. FY27 order inflow guidance is contingent on BHEL orders.
Seamless pipe sold externally expected to earn about 20% margin, lower than captive use.
Middle East reconstruction enquiries not yet received; management said the opportunity is large but too fluid to size.
Fertiliser: one export job being discussed and a possible Namrup job, timing uncertain.
Gross margin decline in Q4 attributed partly to trading activity with about 95-100% material value; no clear commodity-inflation split given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Thailand HRSG order linked to the GE/Siemens/Mitsubishi gas turbine backlog, and does the Rs 150 Cr revenue need capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most orders are linked to the overseas HRSG market. Thailand works on job-work basis, so the Rs 150 Cr figure is mostly value-add rather than full revenue, with EBITDA margin above 20% and only minor capex.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the gross margin decline is commodity inflation versus mix, and what are the alloy and job-work splits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined a quarterly split, citing project-based business, and pointed to trading activity at 95-100% material value in Q4. Job-work orders are about 30% of the book; about 55-60% of thermal and HRSG work is alloy steel.

qa_highlights.question: Are order flows and margins sustainable with the new Anjar and seamless plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Anjar fabrication expected to be near optimal in FY27 and seamless 60-70% utilised. Consolidated EBITDA margin should stay above 19% even if percentage margin falls in heavy fabrication.

qa_highlights.question: Why is order book up about 50% while guidance is 20-25% growth, and why did inventory stay flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance was called conservative; capacity expansion may be needed. Flat inventory despite a higher order book was attributed to power-sector raw material arriving late, after orders were placed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is capex held back given strong HRSG demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is on the drawing board for new capacity, aiming for assets sustainable over 10-15 years, and will publish a blueprint soon.

qa_highlights.question: Malwa Power: how will the qualified audit opinion be resolved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects both plants to be slightly positive at current tariffs, so no impairment or contingency is needed. Audit finding expected to clear by Q3 FY27, per the CFO.

risks_watch: BHEL's slow release of thermal boiler-turbine-generator orders could delay domestic power orders and hit the Rs 2,000 Cr inflow target.
Malwa Power appellate outcome and the qualified audit opinion, expected to clear by Q3 FY27.
Working capital: payable days fell to 42 from a target of 70-75, and inventory days are rising; cycle target differs (180 vs 200 days) across the call.
Order book figure stated as Rs 2,040 Cr by the CEO and Rs 1,940 Cr by the CFO; needs confirmation.
Rising debt and possible equity raise, with no decision yet.
Margin dilution from more material-supply jobs and trading activity; gross margin declined YoY and QoQ.
Dependence on Thailand job-work revenue, which is concentrated in HRSG orders.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the FY27 targets, but evasive on quarterly margin drivers, mix splits and capex size. Management repeatedly called guidance conservative while deferring details on capacity expansion, equity raise and the Middle East opportunity.
key_quotes: Our core business, piping, heavy fabrication, and others continue to be where we generate the most value and margin, and that is evidenced clearly in our full-year operating performance.
But you kindly consider that our console level EBITDA will be above 19% in any case.
Sir, my only request is that these are very, very conservative estimates.
It is still on the drawing board. We shall get back as soon as the decision is taken on that.
